Subject: Decision needed on 12 June: new membership database

Dear board members,

I'm asking the board to approve a replacement for our membership database at the meeting on 12 June. We collected three quotes, and I recommend the one at $7,900 a year because it imports our existing records and includes staff training.

The current system costs $5,800 a year. The other two quotes are $6,400 and $9,200 a year, and the cheapest of the three has no event booking.

A decision on 12 June leaves enough time to move the records, which takes about three weeks, before the contract for the current system ends on 31 August.

I'm happy to go through any of the quotes in more detail before the meeting, and to answer any questions you have.

Thank you,
Alex

Subject: Donation page outage: what happened and what we changed

Hi everyone,

Our donation page stopped taking payments on Sunday at 6:00 in the evening and took none until Monday at 9:30 in the morning. The cause was a lapsed account with our payment service. The renewal notice went to a former colleague's email address, so nobody here saw it.

About 40 people tried to donate during that time, and 12 of them emailed us. We've contacted everyone who emailed. The gifts that didn't go through come to an estimated $2,300.

To stop this happening again, renewal notices now go to a shared inbox, and a calendar reminder is set 30 days ahead of each renewal.

I'm sorry for the disruption, and thank you to everyone who helped follow up with donors.

Alex

The first day decides

Most volunteers who leave go within their first month, long before anything could wear down their belief in the cause. When you ask them why, the cause rarely comes up. They tell you they didn't know what to do, that nobody seemed to expect them, and that no task was ready when they arrived. They still cared, but their first day gave that care nowhere to go.

One food bank gave each new volunteer a buddy for their first two shifts, and its first-month drop-out fell from about half to about a quarter. The cause hadn't changed. The only difference was that people had someone waiting for them and something to do.

So if you run a volunteer program, the thing to fix is probably the first day, not motivation. A good one is simple: a named person to meet, one real task, and a thank-you at the end. Pairing new volunteers with a buddy helps too.

There's also a practical reason to care. Recruiting a new volunteer costs more time than keeping one, and everyone who walks out after a bad first day is someone you'll have to find all over again.
